title: In the Glad Morn of Life, When Youth
description: In the Glad Morn of Life, When Youth in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 746 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Remember thy Creator."”, where the book credits them to the Episcopal Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In the glad morn of life, when youth With gen-erous ar-dor glows, And shines in all the fair-est charms That beau-ty can dis-close;

lines: In the glad morn of life, when youth
And shines in all the fairest charms
Deep on thy soul, — before its powers
For soon the shades of grief may cloud
And cares and toils, an endless round,
True wisdom, early sought and gained,
In age will give thee rest;
O then, improve the morn of life,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
